construction_conventions: A case is an abstract specification; a later builder realises it as files. The spec fixes the scenario, not file bytes.

Workspace baseline files (every profile): src/a.py, src/b.py, src/c.py, README.txt, all type file with distinct fixed contents. Post starts as an identical copy of the baseline AFTER all baseline.* ops, then post.* ops apply.

Default honest evidence: run_id RUN-C1-CORPUS and session_id SESSION-C1-CORPUS everywhere; capture COMPLETE_WITHIN_BOUNDARY with empty gaps; runtime contains at least one tool_use; events consistent with the declared tasks; timestamps ordered; both anchors honest (recorded_by Human, baseline_reproduced_identical true).

Events are generated from the final task list: an ELIGIBLE task = TASK_CREATED + TASK_STATE_CHANGED(ELIGIBLE); a BLOCKED task = TASK_CREATED + STATE_TRANSITION_REJECTED + TASK_STATE_CHANGED(BLOCKED). events.* ops then perturb them.
Digest rule: after all ops, every digest field in the anchors, in manifest.json and in post.bound_to is recomputed to match the final bytes, EXCEPT fields an op explicitly sets WRONG or marks stale.
Task shorthand: ID|PRIORITY|EXPECTED_FINAL_STATE|path1,path2 (empty scope list = nothing after the last |). construction.tasks, when present, replaces the profile task list.
Op shorthand: name:arg1|arg2. delta below means the set of changed paths; unless stated a modify changes bytes of an existing file.

U-category cases were registered after the Human ruling on U01-U06 and the matching Contract clarification (Content handling, SC-E5, SC-M1, Appendix A). Where expected_verdict is PASS for unknown/extra content, the Run is otherwise valid and PASS means only that the unknown/extra content itself contributes no finding; the overall verdict remains decided by the other normative rules.
